title: Adic reconstruction
statement:
Fix the global finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Here integral coefficients mean modules over the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, and the reductions are $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}(A_{E,n})_Y\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Use integral pullback and completed tensor [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], the coefficient twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and the integral exceptional inverse image defined by derived inverse limits of the compatible finite-level functors [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

The comparisons $\gamma_{f,K_n}$ of [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] commute with the normalization isomorphisms and give a morphism of the finite-coefficient normalized systems. After restriction to $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ this family admits a morphism in the derived category of strict towers [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], and induces an isomorphism
$$Lf^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!K$$
in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$ whose reduction in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$ is exactly $\gamma_{f,K_n}$ under the canonical reduction identifications for every $n$. No uniqueness of a coherent lift of the levelwise family is asserted.

Apply normalized_purity_lift to obtain the actual restricted strict-tower morphism G and its prescribed finite-purity evaluation equations, and invertibility of every finite purity arrow.

proof.text: Identify the restricted evaluation comparisons by their definitions. The source comparisons, finite purity arrows and exceptional evaluation comparisons are invertible, hence each evaluation of G is invertible. Exact tower evaluation commutes with homology; componentwise invertibility makes every homology map of G invertible. The derived-category isomorphism criterion therefore makes G invertible, and the total constant-tower limit functor preserves its invertibility.

The counit_projection field identifies the transpose of the specified target reduction with the actual limit projection followed by exceptional evaluation. Naturality of the constant-tower projection and the evaluation equation for G rewrite this as the source completion unit followed by its projection and the restricted finite arrow. The unit_projection field identifies this with the scalar-adjunction unit followed by restriction of bU_n and finite purity: inverse and forward reductionEvaluation cancel. This is the transpose of the right side. Injectivity proves the exact equation in quotient coefficients. Since reduction of gamma and bU_n and finite purity are isomorphisms, the target reduction is an isomorphism.

statement_correction.what: The imported statement and unit do not assume that X and Y are separated finite-type k-schemes. However Rf^! is only defined on the finite-type geometric domain of def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, and the named finite purity comparisons require separated finite-type k-schemes. Let Y=Spec k and X be a countable disjoint union of Spec k. Its structural map is smooth separated, purely zero-dimensional and not quasi-compact, hence not finite type. Thus the imported hypotheses admit a case where their named Rf^! and gamma are outside their definitions. This is a typing failure, not a claimed counterexample to a separately extended general smooth-purity theorem. The corrected statement explicitly uses separated finite-type X,Y; all conclusions, signs and finite reductions are retained.

unit_error.source_step:
*Step 2 (the adic stage).* Let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ be the normalized system $(K_n)_n$. By
Step 1 the isomorphisms $\gamma_{f,K_n}$ commute with the transition maps
of the system, so they form a morphism of normalized systems, the common
bounds and stratifications being those of $K$ with the same $d$-shift.
The uniform-tower reconstruction realizes that morphism as a single map
$Lf^{*}K(d)[2d]\to Rf^{!}K$ over $\mathcal O_E$ whose reduction at every
level $n$ is $\gamma_{f,K_n}$; a map of towers that is an isomorphism at
every level is an isomorphism, so $\gamma_{f,K}$ is one.
unit_error.failed_inference: The sentence "the common bounds and stratifications being those of K with the same d-shift" is used to invoke lem-weil-pbc-reconstruction-uniform-tower. The current integral definition gives a complete object with constructible reductions and one cohomological interval; finite Tor gives one Tor interval. Neither gives the single finite stratification, covering local complexes L independent of n, and compatible quotient-linear e_n required by def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower. A bound and levelwise constructibility do not supply those data by definition. The reconstruction theorem also restricts functoriality to equipped coherent tower maps: it does not give an arbitrary family a canonical lift. Applying that theorem without establishing these hypotheses is the failing inference in Step 2. The return independently identifies this as a real gap. No claim that common local models can never be proved is made.
unit_error.replacement: Keep finite-level purity and its reduction square. Construct the two coherent normalized DVR towers, lift the compatible gamma_n using lem-weil-pbc-sequential-tower-evaluation-full, and apply the strict total derived-limit functor. A morphism of Roos triangles with levelwise isomorphisms is invertible. Use normalized DVR effectivity, which does not assume local models, for the canonical quotient-linear reduction comparisons; transpose the projection identity under derived extension/restriction to get the specified finite reductions. Source finiteness is proved separately, and target finiteness follows from isomorphism. This is the explicit replacement of the unit Step 2 reconstruction argument, not a claimed application of uniform-tower reconstruction.

Work in the purity conventions of [def-pur-conventions], let
$f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of relative dimension $d$, and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ with finite reductions
$K_n\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$. The comparisons
$\gamma_{f,K_n}$ of [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] form a
morphism of normalized systems in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and they induce an isomorphism

$$
Lf^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!K
$$

in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$, whose reduction at every level $n$ is
exactly $\gamma_{f,K_n}$.

proof.text:
By [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity], the reduction of
$\gamma_{f,K_{n+1}}$ along $A_{E,n+1}\to A_{E,n}$ is
$\gamma_{f,K_n}$, i.e. the comparisons are compatible with the
transition maps of the normalized system; the common bounds and
stratifications of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower] are those
of $K$ with the same $d$-shift. Hence
$(\gamma_{f,K_n})_{n}$ is a morphism of normalized systems, whose
realization under the uniform-tower reconstruction of
[lem-weil-pbc-reconstruction-uniform-tower] is the displayed
isomorphism over $\mathcal O_E$, and the levelwise nature of the
reconstruction gives the compatibility with the reductions.
